events.title: Funding Innovation (workshop)
events.location: UF Innovate | Sid Martin Biotech, 12085 Research Dr., Alachua, FL 32615
events.description:
The session combines an educational seminar on SBIR/STTR and other federal funding opportunities with one-on-one office hours, giving participants both a broad understanding of the programs and personalized guidance tailored to their technology and funding goals.
The seminar provides a practical overview of the U.S. non-dilutive funding ecosystem, including:
• Introduction to SBIR/STTR and federal funding opportunities
• Understanding the differences between agencies (NSF, NIH, DoD and others)
• Eligibility requirements and program structure
• How to identify the right agency for your technology
• Proposal writing best practices
• Common pitfalls and how to avoid them
• Funding strategy and commercialization considerations
Participants will also have three 20-minute office hour time slots available after the seminar to discuss:
• Technology fit for SBIR/STTR
• Agency selection
• Funding strategy
• Proposal readiness
• Next steps and commercialization pathway
After registering for the event, you’ll find the available time slots listed in your confirmation email.About our speakers:Fernando Hernandez
Fernando Hernandez serves as the Vice President of Sales & Operations at Inspiralia US, where he leads business development and strategic partnerships. In this role, he collaborates closely with startups, universities, incubators, and innovation ecosystems to help organizations identify, pursue, and secure federal funding opportunities that support research, innovation, and growth.Berta Okenve
Berta Okenve serves as the Head of Industry & Health Projects at Inspiralia US, where she specializes in helping innovative companies secure public funding for research and development. With experience supporting more than 100 U.S. and European organizations, Berta has extensive expertise in Life Sciences, Biotechnology, Healthcare, and navigating funding opportunities through the National Institutes of Health (NIH), helping clients successfully access non-dilutive funding to advance their innovations.About our sponsor:Inspiralia
Inspiralia is an innovation funding consultancy specializing in SBIR/STTR programs, federal grants, innovation funding strategy, and commercialization support. The firm partners with startups, universities, and research organizations to identify funding opportunities, develop competitive grant proposals, and manage the entire funding process—from opportunity identification through award management.Thank you to our sponsor:———————UF Innovate | Accelerate
UF Innovate | Accelerate is the University of Florida’s entrepreneurship support program that includes Sid Martin Biotech, the globally recognized biotechnology incubator located in Progress Park in Alachua, Florida, and The Hub, the globally recognized diversified tech incubator located in Gainesville’s Innovation District.

events.title: The Florida Way Forward
events.location: University of Florida, 655 Reitz Union Drive, Gainesville, FL 32603
events.description:
Standing InnOvation is UF Innovate | Tech Licensing’s annual celebration recognizing University of Florida researchers who have disclosed, optioned, or licensed technologies or received issued patents during FY26. This is an invite-only event that honors the outstanding contributions of UF innovators across disciplines.
While Standing InnOvation is invite-only, the keynote is free and open to the public. The program begins with a keynote from Patric Young, former Florida Gator standout, professional basketball player, and current ESPN SEC Network analyst.
Through his story of resilience and perseverance, he demonstrates how setbacks can create opportunities for growth and how progress is not always linear. His journey reflects what it means to embrace the Florida Way Forward and keep moving ahead, no matter the challenge.Click here to register for the keynote session. (https://luma.com/m00jg6q6)
About the speaker: Patric Young
Patric Young is a former Florida Gator basketball player, professional basketball player, ESPN SEC Network analyst, author, motivational speaker, and founder of the Patric Young Foundation (https://www.py4foundation.org/). Patric played for the Florida Gators from 2010 to 2014 before beginning his professional basketball career.
After an accident left him paralyzed from the waist down, he began a new chapter focused on resilience, perseverance, and purpose. Today, Patric shares his story through speaking, writing, and his work with the Patric Young Foundation. His experience shows that setbacks can change your path without defining your future.

events.title: From Bench To Automation (Lunch & Learn)
events.location: UF Innovate | Sid Martin Biotech, 12085 Research Dr., Alachua, FL 32615
events.description:
From 11 AM – 1 PM in the Sid Martin main lobby, attendees are invited to stop by for lunch, refreshments, and conversation with our laboratory automation specialists. Rather than focusing on a single application or product, the session is designed around the work being done by companies within the Sid Martin community.
Bring us your workflow. Whether you are working with PCR and qPCR, NGS, genomics, cell-based assays, sample preparation, assay development, plate-based workflows, reagent dispensing, normalization, dilution series, or another application, we can discuss how automation could potentially fit into your process.
The goal is to help answer questions such as:
– What parts of my current workflow can realistically be automated?
– When does automation make sense and when does it not?
– How can automation improve reproducibility and consistency?
– Can automation help reduce hands-on time or increase throughput?
– How do you translate an existing manual protocol into an automated workflow?
– What should a lab consider before implementing liquid handling automation?
An Eppendorf automated liquid handling platform will be available so attendees can see the technology and discuss specific applications with the team.
Following the Lunch & Learn, from approximately 1 – 1:30 PM, Eppendorf will host a more focused 20-30 minute educational presentation in the conference room covering the fundamentals of laboratory automation, common applications, workflow development, and considerations when transitioning from manual pipetting to automated liquid handling. Meet with Phillip Tender and Taylor Smith of Eppendorf.
Terrie Gunter of USA Scientific will also be onsite during the event to meet with attendees and support discussions around laboratory workflows, consumables, and automation applications.About our speakers:Philip Tendler
Philip Tendler supports laboratory automation and floor model centrifugation technologies throughout the Southeastern United States for Eppendorf North America. With a graduate background in molecular genetics from the University of Georgia and experience working with academic, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and research laboratories, Philip focuses on helping scientists evaluate technologies that can improve workflow efficiency, reproducibility, throughput, and overall laboratory productivity.Taylor Smith
Taylor Smith is an Application Integration Specialist with Eppendorf North America, specializing in automated liquid handling applications and workflow development. Taylor works directly with scientists to understand existing laboratory protocols, identify opportunities for automation, and translate manual processes into reliable automated workflows. During the event, Taylor will be available to discuss individual applications and the practical considerations involved in developing automated methods. Thank you to our sponsors:

 ———————UF Innovate | Accelerate

Join us for an evening of celebration of the individuals and companies that are driving North Central Florida’s thriving startup and innovation ecosystem. celebrateGNV brings together entrepreneurs, mentors, business leaders, and community builders for an inspiring dinner event recognizing those who are making a real difference in our region.

• Community Impact Company of the Year – Recognizing established companies making a meaningful difference in our region

Whether you’re a startup founder, seasoned entrepreneur, mentor, or simply passionate about innovation in North Central Florida, this is your opportunity to celebrate achievements, connect with like-minded professionals, and be inspired by the incredible work happening in our community.

Come raise a glass to the people and organizations making North Central Florida a premier destination for startups and innovation!

events.title: Off The Couch Book Tour + Fireside Chat
events.location: UF Innovate | The Hub, 747 SW Second Avenue, Gainesville, FL 32607
events.description:
About the book:
Off The Couch is the story of what happens when service becomes a habit instead of an assignment. It traces a path from the discipline of the United States Air Force to the messy, hopeful work of building startup ecosystems in places that were told they’d never have one.
Along the way, Robert unpacks the practical machinery of resilience: how to keep moving when the plan collapses, how to turn data and hard truths into better decisions, and how to build the kind of network that catches founders before they fall.
Part memoir, part playbook, this book (https://robertblacklidge.com/off-the-couch) is written for the person still sitting on the couch — the veteran in transition, the founder waiting for permission, the community leader wondering whether one person can move an entire ecosystem forward. The answer, gathered across hundreds of pitches, mentors, and midnight launches, is yes.About our speaker:Robert Blacklidge
Robert Blacklidge is an educator, technology strategist, and veteran with over twenty years of experience spanning military service, enterprise data architecture, and academic leadership. As a startup mentor and ecosystem builder, he has guided over 100 founders through venture validation and scaling. Read more here.
